paper_metadata.title: Financial Fraud Detection with Entropy Computing

summary: Introduces CVQBoost, a continuous-variable quadratic boosting classifier solved on QCi's Dirac-3 Entropy Quantum Computing (EQC) photonic device. Benchmarked on the Kaggle Credit Card Fraud Detection dataset (~200k European transactions, ~0.1% fraud, 38 features) against XGBoost. Two experiments: (1) downsampling + oversampling study (ADASYN, SMOTE, SMOTE-SVM, majority downsampling at ratios {0.01, 0.02, 0.05, 0.1, 0.5, 1.0}) measuring test AUC - CVQBoost is competitive but generally lags XGBoost (e.g., ratio 1.0: 0.8508 vs 0.8872); (2) training-time scaling on 1K-150K Kaggle samples (38 features) and 1M-70M synthetic samples with 100-900 features - CVQBoost shows near-constant train time (~1-3 s) while XGBoost scales roughly linearly (117 s at 150k samples), suggesting a practical training-time advantage at scale on Dirac-3.

experiments.description: Credit-card fraud classification AUC as a function of class-balancing ratio. Kaggle dataset (~200k, ~0.1% fraud, 38 features). Balancing schemes: ADASYN, SMOTE, SMOTE-SVM oversampling + majority-class downsampling to ratios r in {0.01, 0.02, 0.05, 0.1, 0.5, 1.0}. CVQBoost (on Dirac-3 EQC photonic device) vs XGBoost baseline; metric: AUC on held-out test set.

algorithm.variant: CVQBoost - continuous-variable quadratic boosting; weak-learner weights optimized as a continuous QUBO-like quadratic program on the QCi Dirac-3 Entropy Quantum Computing photonic device
algorithm.ansatz: Continuous-variable quadratic objective solved natively by Dirac-3 photonic EQC (not a gate circuit); classed as 'other' since EQC is neither standard annealing nor gate-based.
algorithm.optimizer: Dirac-3 Entropy Quantum Computing solver (photonic, continuous-variable)

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Boosting aggregation expressed as a continuous quadratic objective over weak-learner weights; submitted directly to Dirac-3 photonic EQC.
problem_formulation.constraints: continuous, non-negative weight budget on weak learners

dataset_specification.benchmark_name: Kaggle Credit Card Fraud Detection (European cardholders, Sept 2013)
dataset_specification.description: ~200,000 transactions, ~0.1% fraud class, 38 features (PCA-transformed + Amount/Time). Highly imbalanced binary classification.

results.notes: Table 1, CVQBoost on Dirac-3, downsampling ratio 0.05.

speedup_claims.notes: On AUC alone, CVQBoost does not beat XGBoost at any reported ratio; paper's advantage claim is on training time (see experiment 2).

notes: AUC values read from Table 1 of arXiv:2503.11273. Dirac-3 is QCi's photonic Entropy Quantum Computing device; we classify it as real_qpu_photonic and algorithm.family='other' because its continuous-variable optimization model does not map cleanly to either quantum-annealing (Ising) or gate-based circuits.

experiments.description: Training-time scaling study on the Kaggle dataset (38 features) for sample counts 1K, 20K, 50K, 100K, 150K; extended (in paper's discussion) to 1M-70M synthetic samples with 100-900 features. Metric: wall-clock training time in seconds. CVQBoost on Dirac-3 vs XGBoost on CPU.

dataset_specification.description: Training-set sweep: 1K-150K real samples, then 1M-70M synthetic samples.

speedup_claims.notes: CVQBoost training on Dirac-3 is near-constant (~1-3 s) while XGBoost scales roughly linearly with dataset size: 117.4 s vs 2.2 s at 150k samples (~53x). Paper further demonstrates scaling to 70M x 900-feature synthetic data where CVQBoost remains tractable.

complexity_analysis.quantum_complexity: near-constant empirical training time on Dirac-3 across tested sizes
complexity_analysis.classical_complexity: approximately linear in sample count for XGBoost

advantage_assessment.crossover_size: ~20k samples (where XGBoost training time exceeds CVQBoost on Dirac-3)

notes: Training times read from Table 2 of arXiv:2503.11273. Note that AUC (experiment 1) remains below XGBoost, so the claimed advantage is in training throughput, not predictive quality.
